user.title: Connect the judge (runtime decisions)
user.description:
This integration asks a **fast discriminative model** what state the house is in. The default is Jev (`api.typesafe.ai`), but endpoint, model name and key are all yours to change — anything speaking the same request shape can replace it.

**What happens next**: we send one very short probe (its content is only "did this message arrive?", no home data) to confirm the endpoint answers — and you pay the 1–2s cross-border TLS handshake now, while filling a form, instead of during a night-time trigger.

**About how this key is stored, said up front**: Home Assistant keeps integration config in plaintext under `.storage/` (mode 0644); the platform gives custom integrations no way to encrypt it. What we can promise: it never reaches logs or traces, it is always redacted in the diagnostics export, and we never handle it. Do not put a long-lived token on a shared machine or one whose backups others can read.

data_description.decision_base_url: Defaults to `https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone`. A self-hosted endpoint must answer the same request shape (`state`/`questions`) — not every inference server does.
data_description.decision_model: Like `jev-latest`. Empty falls back to the default.
data_description.decision_key: Looks like `apikey_…`. A wrong one is not saved: the next step verifies it.

compiler.title: Connect the compiler (ideas → policies)
compiler.description:
The second model role: **you write what you want in plain words, the compiler turns it into a policy draft**, you review it on a form, trial it, and only then is it saved. The judge has only three discriminative primitives and no generation ability, so this step needs another model — any endpoint speaking OpenAI-compatible `chat/completions`, including one running on this machine.

**You can skip it**: leave URL and model empty and the judge still works at runtime; the cost is that "add a policy from a sentence" stays unavailable until you configure it.

data_description.compiler_base_url: e.g. `https://api.openai.com/v1`, or local `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1`. `host:port` alone works too — we add the scheme.
data_description.compiler_model: e.g. `gpt-4o-mini`, `qwen2.5:14b`. It has to be able to emit plain JSON.
data_description.compiler_key: Local endpoints usually need none; leave it empty.

error.auth_failed: The judge rejected this key (auth failed). Check it is not expired, has no stray spaces, or try another one.
error.timeout: The judge did not answer in time. This happens on slow cross-border links — retry once; if it keeps failing, check that this machine can reach that endpoint.
error.unreachable: Cannot reach the judge endpoint. Check network, DNS, or a local proxy blocking the domain.
error.http_error: The judge returned an error status. Retry later; if it persists check the provider status page.
error.bad_url: That endpoint URL is unusable. Write it as `http://host:port/v1` or `https://example.com/v1`, with the scheme.
error.compiler_bad: The compiler did not pass this check. Likely causes: wrong URL or model name, the endpoint does not serve `chat/completions`, or it wraps JSON in prose. You can skip and configure it later.
error.compile_failed: This idea did not compile into a policy. The reason is below.
error.draft_invalid: Your change made the draft invalid; the reason is below.

abort.already_configured: This Home Assistant already has one instance configured. **Adding another piece of smart control does not mean installing again**: open this integration's Configure dialog and add a policy from a sentence. A second instance would make "which threshold is live" two sources of truth.
abort.not_ready: The integration is not running right now (bad config or reloading). Fix that before managing policies.

init.title: Smart controls

pick.title: Pick a policy
pick.description: Each entry is its own "when to look, which readings, what to ask, whether to act". When two policies point at the same device, **the later verdict wins**, but the override is always traced — never silent.

delete_confirm.title: Confirm delete
delete_confirm.description: This deletes “{策略}”. Its history stays in the local `traces/` file, but the policy itself cannot be restored.

data_description.confirm: It is only deleted if you choose "delete".

add.title: Add a smart control from a sentence

data_description.intent: e.g. After sunset, if I am still awake put the bedside lamp on dimmest; if I am catching up on sleep, do nothing.
data_description.entities: At least one. Tick only what is genuinely relevant: the more you give, the more room the compiler has to be wrong.

review.title: Review the draft

data.name: Policy name
data.question: The question to ask the model

data_description.question: This sentence goes to the model verbatim. The criteria are what it actually judges by — visible in the summary.
data_description.threshold: For yes/no it is the probability boundary; for choice/ordinal it is a confidence floor — below it, nothing is executed. Chinese phrasing measures about 0.1 lower than English, so do not copy 0.5 blindly.
data_description.action_entity: Only entities from the candidate set you just ticked.
data_description.cooldown: Minimum gap between two actions from this same policy. Most "the house is twitchy" complaints live here.

trial.title: Trial: real judgement, real action
trial.description:
A trial is **not a rehearsal**: this run really asks the model {次数} times, and if an action branch matches it really operates that device (ADR-0005). Only this draft is fed in, so other policies are not touched.

**This round**

{结果}

Adjusting the threshold is meant to be looked at again right here. Save when you are satisfied — saving is itself the confirmation.

data_description.threshold: Change it and choose "try again" — no need to go back a step.
data_description.next: Once saved, this policy takes part in everyday judgement immediately.

settings.title: Global settings
settings.description: Both model endpoints and the budget for one judgement. Saving reloads the integration — a run in flight is discarded rather than leaving half an action behind.

data_description.decision_key: Empty means "keep it". To replace the key, paste the whole string — the field never shows the stored value.
data_description.compiler_key: Empty means "keep it". Local endpoints usually stay empty.
data_description.timeout_seconds: Measured on a direct cross-border link: median 1.4s, peak 2.6s, and the very first request after a cold connect is the tightest. Over budget triggers the safety fallback instead of hanging.

abort.not_ready: The integration is not running right now (bad config or reloading). Fix that before managing policies.

error.auth_failed: The judge rejected this key. Nothing was saved — fix it and try again.
error.timeout: The judge didn't answer in time. Nothing was saved — check that this machine can reach the endpoint.
error.unreachable: Cannot reach the judge endpoint. Nothing was saved: check network, DNS or a local proxy.
error.http_error: The judge returned an error status. Nothing was saved; retry later or switch back.
error.bad_url: Unusable endpoint URL. Write it as `http://host:port/v1` or `https://example.com/v1`.
error.compiler_bad: The compiler failed this check (URL, model name, or it does not serve `chat/completions`). Nothing was saved.
